subject: Identifying a host's own plug-in instances across Mixer strips and editor windows through the accessibility tree
question: Can a read-only walk of the docked Mixer and the open plug-in editor windows join a plug-in's instances to the strips that host them, using the kAXIdentifier the plug-in's own view sets, without any action on Logic?

reverify.command: link LogicProMCPKit from a host application that sets kAXIdentifier <prefix><instance-id> on its AUv3 view root; open a project with the Mixer docked (X) and N instances with their editor windows open; call AXPluginInstanceIdentity.census(pluginName:identifierPrefix:) from an unsandboxed process with Accessibility granted
reverify.expected: strips.count == N with stripsReadWhole true, windows.count == N, every window carrying an identifier with the prefix, and each window title equal to the hosting strip's name
reverify.cost: ~5 min with the consumer application installed; needs Logic in front with a disposable project and Accessibility granted to the reading process

method: The consumer application (an AUv3 host, SN8K) linked the LogicProMCPKit product pinned at e01c8e8c and called the census every 2 s from an unsandboxed container process with Accessibility granted, on the operator's desk: Logic Pro 12.3.1 with a 23-track project, the Mixer docked in the main window (X) with the header set to All, six instances of the plug-in on six non-contiguous strips, and all six editor windows open. The consumer's own trace recorded the census summary, the join, and the six resulting bindings; the plug-in's view stamped kAXIdentifier sn8k.instance:<instance-uuid> on its root. Separately, a direct accessibility walk from a trusted shell process read each editor window's title and identifiers, each occupied insert slot's description, and the Mixer's layout items in both layouts (docked, and as a standalone window). Track and project names were read to decide but were not recorded; the receipts carry instance uuids, ordinals, channels and counts only.

canon_not_applicable.reason: This record measures accessibility-tree behaviour (which window carries a host-set identifier, what an editor window's title equals, where the Mixer's strips are reachable, and how a slot label is truncated), not a string shipped in Logic's canonical data.

observations.what: census on the operator's desk, Mixer docked, six instances, six windows open
editor windows whose kAXIdentifier carried the host's prefix
editor windows whose AX title equalled the hosting strip's name field
bindings formed from the join, one per instance
occupied insert slots labelled with the AU component name truncated to ten characters
Mixer strips found by getMixerArea, by layout
kAXErrorCannotComplete on the first windows read after a Logic start, recovered by one re-read

conclusion: On this host a read-only census joined all six plug-in instances to their strips: 6 of 6 editor windows carried the host-set identifier, 6 of 6 window titles equalled the hosting strip's name, and 6 bindings formed at offset 0 from 1 anchor. The Mixer's strips were reachable only with the Mixer docked; the standalone Mixer window reported mixerFound false. Insert slots carried the component name truncated to ten characters (6 of 6). A -25204 on the first windows read recovered after one 200 ms re-read.
limits: One host: Logic Pro 12.3.1 build 6682, macOS 26.6.2, UI language en-US, one project, one plug-in (SN8K, an AUv3). Other plug-in formats, other hosts of the library, and the other nine declared locales are not measured here.

The window title equalling the track name is an observed behaviour of 12.3.1; the join by title is the caller's, and two tracks with the same name are the caller's ambiguity to refuse, not this record's finding.

Reads were issued from an unsandboxed process. A sandboxed process gets kAXErrorCannotComplete on every read of another application while AXIsProcessTrusted() is true; that failure mode was measured on the same desk and is why the consumer runs unsandboxed.
The standalone Mixer window was found by a direct walk of all windows but not by getMixerArea; this record does not verify a locator for it.

The six formed lines are the consumer's trace, not this library's output; the census itself returned the counts in the first observation, and the receipts carry uuids and ordinals only, with no track names.
